test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated user is redirected to login when accessing the Forecast page
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a browser with no active session.
2. Navigate directly to /sprints/SPRINT-x/forecast/.
test_cases.expected: The user is redirected to the login page. No forecast data or team information is visible.

test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user can access the Sprint Forecast page
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Planning > Sprints.
3. Open a sprint detail page.
4. Click the Forecast button in the sprint detail page actions.
test_cases.expected: The Sprint Forecast page loads. The page title reads '{Sprint Name} — Forecast'. The Teams panel is visible with accordion rows for each active team.

test_cases.scenario: Import button is not visible to users without the import_forecast permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without the sprints.import_forecast permission.
2. Open the Sprint Forecast page.
test_cases.expected: No Import button appears on any team accordion row. The file input element is not rendered in the page.

test_cases.scenario: Import button is visible to users with the import_forecast permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with the sprints.import_forecast permission.
2. Open the Sprint Forecast page.
test_cases.expected: An Import button (with upload icon) is visible on every team accordion row header.

test_cases.scenario: Review Complete button is initially disabled and enables after a team is confirmed
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page for a sprint where no team has a confirmed import.
2. Observe the Review Complete button state.
test_cases.expected: The Review Complete button is disabled. After at least one team confirms an import, the button becomes enabled.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint Forecast page is inaccessible for a closed sprint
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Forecast page for a sprint whose status is Closed.
test_cases.expected: The Teams panel shows a locked state: a lock icon, the message 'Sprint is closed', and a description that forecast data cannot be imported. The Import button is not rendered.

test_cases.scenario: Page title updates to include the sprint name after loading
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page.
2. Wait for the page to finish loading.
test_cases.expected: The page title changes from 'Forecast' to '{Sprint Name} — Forecast'. The breadcrumbs update to show: Project / Planning / Sprints / {Sprint Name} / Forecast.

test_cases.scenario: Loading spinner is shown while teams are being fetched
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page on a throttled network.
2. Observe the Teams panel immediately after the page loads.
test_cases.expected: A loading spinner with the text 'Loading teams…' is shown inside the Teams panel until the API responds.

test_cases.scenario: Empty state is shown when there are no active teams
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Sprint Forecast page for an instance where no active teams exist.
test_cases.expected: The Teams panel shows an empty state with a people icon and the message 'No active teams found.'

test_cases.scenario: Download Template button is always visible regardless of permissions
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as any authenticated user.
2. Open the Sprint Forecast page.
test_cases.expected: The Download Template button is visible in the page header actions for all authenticated users.

test_cases.scenario: Each active team appears as a separate accordion row
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page for a sprint.
2. Count the accordion rows in the Teams panel.
test_cases.expected: One accordion row is shown per active team. Inactive teams are not listed.

test_cases.scenario: Team status badge shows Active (blue) when the latest import is not confirmed
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV for a team without confirming it.
2. Return to the Sprint Forecast page.
test_cases.expected: The team's accordion row shows an 'Active' badge in blue next to the team name.

test_cases.scenario: Team status badge shows Confirmed (green) when the latest import is confirmed
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload and confirm a forecast import for a team.
2. Return to the Sprint Forecast page.
test_cases.expected: The team's accordion row shows a 'Confirmed' badge in green next to the team name.

test_cases.scenario: Team status badge shows Superseded (grey) for an older import replaced by a newer one
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload and confirm a forecast import for a team.
2. Upload a second CSV for the same team.
3. Open the import history table for that team.
test_cases.expected: The first import shows a 'Superseded' badge. The second import shows 'Active'.

test_cases.scenario: Expanding an accordion row shows the import history table
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page.
2. Click to expand a team accordion row.
test_cases.expected: The accordion body expands to reveal the import history table with columns: Version, File Name, Status, Imported At, Imported By.

test_cases.scenario: Import history shows empty state when no imports exist for the team
test_cases.steps: 1. Expand a team accordion that has had no files uploaded.
test_cases.expected: The import history table shows the empty message 'No forecast data imported yet for this team.'

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Import on a team accordion header triggers the file picker
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with import_forecast permission.
2. Open the Sprint Forecast page.
3. Click the Import button on any team row (without expanding the accordion).
test_cases.expected: A file picker opens. Clicking Import does not expand or collapse the accordion.

test_cases.scenario: Download Template button initiates a file download
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page.
2. Click the Download Template button.
test_cases.expected: A CSV file is downloaded. The file contains the expected column headers for the forecast import format.

test_cases.scenario: Downloaded template is specific to the current sprint
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page for sprint S1.
2. Download the template.
3. Open the Sprint Forecast page for sprint S2.
4. Download the template.
test_cases.expected: Each download produces a template file scoped to its respective sprint (e.g. may include the sprint code in metadata or filename).

test_cases.scenario: Valid CSV file uploads successfully and the import history table refreshes
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with import_forecast permission.
2. On the Sprint Forecast page, click Import on a team.
3. Select a valid CSV file from the file picker.
test_cases.expected: A success toast appears: 'Forecast uploaded — The file has been recorded successfully.' The team's import history table refreshes and shows the new import as version v1 (or next version) with status Active.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading a second CSV creates a new version and supersedes the previous one
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV for a team (v1, Active).
2. Upload a second CSV for the same team.
test_cases.expected: The first import changes status to Superseded. The second import appears as the new Active version. The team's status badge updates to Active.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading a non-CSV file shows an error
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Import on a team.
2. Select a non-CSV file (e.g. a PNG or XLSX).
test_cases.expected: An error toast is displayed. The import history table does not gain a new entry.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading an empty CSV file shows an error
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Import on a team.
2. Select a CSV file with no data rows (headers only or fully empty).
test_cases.expected: An error toast is displayed with a relevant error message. No new import record is created.

test_cases.scenario: Upload error shows the API error message in the toast
test_cases.steps:
1. Simulate an API failure during upload (e.g. by temporarily disabling the server or submitting a malformed file).
2. Observe the toast message.
test_cases.expected: The error toast displays the message returned by the API. The toast type is 'error'.

test_cases.scenario: The same CSV file can be re-selected after a previous upload attempt
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV for a team.
2. Immediately click Import again and select the same file.
test_cases.expected: The file picker accepts the same file. The upload proceeds and creates a new version. The file input is reset between uploads.

test_cases.scenario: Import history table shows correct columns and data
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV for a team.
2. Expand the team accordion.
test_cases.expected: The import history table shows: Version (e.g. v1), File Name (CSV filename), Status badge, Imported At (formatted date/time), Imported By (user display name or email).

test_cases.scenario: Clicking an import history row navigates to the import detail page
test_cases.steps:
1. Expand a team accordion with at least one import.
2. Click any row in the import history table.
test_cases.expected: The user is navigated to the forecast import detail page at /sprints/{code}/forecast/{import_code}/.

test_cases.scenario: Multiple imports are listed in order with most recent version last
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload two CSV files for the same team.
2. Expand the accordion and inspect the import history table.
test_cases.expected: Both imports are listed. The version numbers increment correctly (v1, v2). The table is readable and does not show duplicate rows.

test_cases.scenario: Review Complete drawer shows a loading state while checking team statuses
test_cases.steps:
1. On the Sprint Forecast page, click Review Complete.
2. Observe the drawer immediately after it opens.
test_cases.expected: A loading spinner is shown with the text 'Checking team statuses…'. The drawer body is hidden until the API responds.

test_cases.scenario: Review Complete drawer shows 'all confirmed' message when every team has a confirmed import
test_cases.steps:
1. Confirm the forecast import for every team in the sprint.
2. Click Review Complete.
test_cases.expected: After loading, the drawer shows a green success message: 'All teams have confirmed forecast imports.' The Complete button is enabled.

test_cases.scenario: Review Complete drawer lists teams with unconfirmed imports
test_cases.steps:
1. Leave at least one team without a confirmed import.
2. Click Review Complete.
test_cases.expected: The drawer lists the unconfirmed teams by name. The message reads 'The following teams do not have a confirmed forecast import for this sprint:'. The Complete button is disabled until the Override checkbox is ticked.

test_cases.scenario: Review Complete requires Override checkbox to proceed when teams are unconfirmed
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Review Complete drawer with at least one unconfirmed team.
2. Attempt to click Complete without ticking the Override checkbox.
test_cases.expected: The Complete button remains disabled. The Override checkbox must be ticked before Complete becomes active.

test_cases.scenario: Notes field in the Review Complete drawer accepts free text
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Review Complete drawer.
2. Type a message in the Notes field.
3. Click Complete.
test_cases.expected: The notes are submitted with the review complete action. No validation error is shown for the Notes field — it is optional.

test_cases.scenario: Review Complete succeeds with override when teams are unconfirmed
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Review Complete drawer with one unconfirmed team.
2. Tick the Override checkbox.
3. Enter a note.
4. Click Complete.
test_cases.expected: The review complete action is submitted. A success toast appears. The sprint's forecast is marked as review complete.

test_cases.scenario: Review Complete drawer can be cancelled without submitting
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Review Complete drawer.
2. Click Cancel.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No review complete action is submitted. The sprint status is unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Import detail page loads with correct title and breadcrumbs
test_cases.steps:
1. From the Sprint Forecast page, click an import history row.
2. Wait for the detail page to load.
test_cases.expected: The page title shows '{Sprint Name} — Forecast Import — v{N}'. Breadcrumbs show: Project / Planning / Sprints / {Sprint Name} / Forecast / Import v{N}.

test_cases.scenario: Page actions show Review, Add Row, and Confirm buttons
test_cases.steps: 1. Open a forecast import detail page.
test_cases.expected: Three buttons are visible in the page actions: 'Add Row', 'Review', and 'Confirm'. Confirm is initially disabled.

test_cases.scenario: Rows tab is active by default on the import detail page
test_cases.steps: 1. Open a forecast import detail page.
test_cases.expected: The Rows tab is the active tab. The rows table is visible. The Engineer Capacity tab is also present.

test_cases.scenario: Confirmed import shows locked state — action buttons are disabled
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the import detail page for an import that is already confirmed.
test_cases.expected: The Review, Add Row, and Confirm buttons are disabled. Row-level Edit and Delete actions are hidden. The import is read-only.

test_cases.scenario: Rows table shows all columns from the uploaded CSV
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV with data rows.
2. Open the import detail page.
test_cases.expected: The Rows table shows: Story Type, Jira ID, Title, Assignee, Efforts, Days, Sprint, Label, Mapping, and Checks columns. All rows from the CSV are present.

test_cases.scenario: Rows table shows 'No rows found' when the import has no rows
test_cases.steps:
1. Create an import with no rows.
2. Open the import detail page.
test_cases.expected: The rows table shows the empty message 'No rows found for this import.'

test_cases.scenario: Checks column shows a dash before review has been run
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import detail page for a newly uploaded import.
2. Inspect the Checks column without running Review.
test_cases.expected: Every row's Checks cell shows a muted dash (—). No check icons appear until Review is run.

test_cases.scenario: Search field filters rows by keyword
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import detail page with multiple rows.
2. Type a keyword in the search field (e.g. a Jira ID or title).
test_cases.expected: The rows table filters to show only matching rows. Non-matching rows are hidden.

test_cases.scenario: Check Type filter narrows rows to those with a specific failing check
test_cases.steps:
1. Run Review on an import with at least one row failing the Assignee check.
2. Select 'Assignee' from the Check Type dropdown.
test_cases.expected: Only rows with a failing Assignee check are shown. Rows that passed all checks or have other failing checks are hidden.

test_cases.scenario: Running Review updates the Checks column for all rows
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import detail page.
2. Click the Review button.
3. Wait for the review to complete.
test_cases.expected: Every row's Checks column is updated. Rows that pass all checks show a green tick. Rows with failures show red icons corresponding to which checks failed.

test_cases.scenario: Assignee check fails and highlights the Assignee cell in red
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV where one row has an assignee name that does not match any active member.
2. Run Review.
test_cases.expected: The Assignee cell for that row is highlighted in red bold text. The Checks cell shows the assignee-not-found icon. Hovering the icon shows the tooltip 'Assignee not found or inactive'.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint check fails and highlights the Sprint cell in red
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV where one row has a sprint name that does not match any active sprint.
2. Run Review.
test_cases.expected: The Sprint cell for that row is highlighted in red. The Checks cell shows the sprint-not-found icon with tooltip 'Sprint not found or inactive'.

test_cases.scenario: Label check fails and highlights the Label cell in red
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV where one row references a project label that does not exist in the system.
2. Run Review.
test_cases.expected: The Label cell for that row is highlighted in red. The Checks cell shows the label-not-found icon with tooltip 'Label not found in system'.

test_cases.scenario: Mapping check fails and highlights the Mapping cell in red
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV where one row has a recharge type mapping that is invalid for the label's project type.
2. Run Review.
test_cases.expected: The Mapping cell for that row is highlighted in red. The Checks cell shows the mapping-invalid icon with tooltip 'Mapping invalid for project type'.

test_cases.scenario: Rows that pass all checks show a green tick
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV with at least one fully valid row.
2. Run Review.
test_cases.expected: Rows where all four checks pass show a single green tick icon in the Checks column. No red icons appear for those rows.

test_cases.scenario: Re-running Review after editing a row updates the check result
test_cases.steps:
1. Run Review — one row fails the Assignee check.
2. Edit that row to set a valid assignee.
3. Run Review again.
test_cases.expected: The Assignee check for the edited row now passes. The Checks column updates to a green tick if all checks pass.

test_cases.scenario: Confirm button becomes enabled after review is run
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import detail page.
2. Observe Confirm button — it is disabled.
3. Click Review and wait for completion.
test_cases.expected: After Review completes, the Confirm button becomes enabled regardless of whether checks passed or failed.

suites.name: Forecast Import Detail — Engineer Capacity Tab

test_cases.scenario: Engineer Capacity tab is accessible after first review is run
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import detail page.
2. Click the Engineer Capacity tab before running Review.
test_cases.expected: The tab is present but shows no capacity data until Review has been run. After running Review, the tab populates with engineer rows.

test_cases.scenario: Capacity tab shows each engineer's net capacity and allocated days
test_cases.steps:
1. Run Review on an import.
2. Click the Engineer Capacity tab.
test_cases.expected: Each engineer in the team is listed with their Net Capacity (days) and Allocated (days) from the import rows.

test_cases.scenario: Capacity check shows green tick when allocated days equal net capacity
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV where an engineer's rows total exactly their net sprint capacity.
2. Run Review.
3. Check the Engineer Capacity tab.
test_cases.expected: That engineer's Checks cell shows a green tick icon with tooltip 'Capacity fully allocated'.

test_cases.scenario: Capacity check shows red icon when allocated days are less than net capacity
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV where an engineer's rows total less than their net sprint capacity.
2. Run Review.
3. Check the Engineer Capacity tab.
test_cases.expected: That engineer's Checks cell shows a red icon with tooltip 'Allocated days less than net capacity'.

test_cases.scenario: Search in Engineer Capacity tab filters engineers by name
test_cases.steps:
1. Run Review.
2. Click the Engineer Capacity tab.
3. Type a partial engineer name in the search field.
test_cases.expected: Only engineers whose names match the search term are shown.

suites.name: Forecast Import Detail — Add, Edit, Delete Rows

test_cases.scenario: Add Row drawer opens with all expected fields
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import detail page.
2. Click Add Row.
test_cases.expected: A drawer opens titled 'Add Row' with fields: Story Type, Jira ID, Title, Assignee (searchable), Efforts (seconds), Sprint, Label, and Mapping.

test_cases.scenario: Submitting a valid Add Row form creates a new row in the table
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Add Row.
2. Fill in Story Type, Title, Assignee, Efforts, Sprint, Label, and Mapping.
3. Click Add Row in the drawer.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The new row appears in the Rows table. A success toast is shown.

test_cases.scenario: Add Row drawer can be cancelled without saving
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Add Row.
2. Fill in some fields.
3. Click Cancel.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No new row is added to the table.

test_cases.scenario: Edit Row drawer pre-populates all fields from the existing row
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the Edit action on any row.
2. Inspect the drawer fields.
test_cases.expected: The Edit Row drawer opens with all fields pre-filled with the row's current values.

test_cases.scenario: Saving an edited row updates it in the table
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Edit on a row.
2. Change the Title field.
3. Click Save Changes.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The row in the table reflects the updated Title. A success toast is shown.

test_cases.scenario: Delete Row confirmation modal appears before deletion
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Delete action on any row.
test_cases.expected: A delete confirmation modal opens with the row's title. The user must confirm before deletion proceeds.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming delete removes the row from the table
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a row.
2. Confirm the deletion.
test_cases.expected: The row is removed from the Rows table. A success toast is shown. The deletion cannot be undone.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling delete does not remove the row
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a row.
2. Click Cancel in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The row remains in the table unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming an import with all checks passed does not require override notes
test_cases.steps:
1. Run Review on an import with no check failures.
2. Click Confirm.
test_cases.expected: The Confirm drawer opens with a message indicating all checks passed. The Override Notes field is hidden. Clicking Confirm in the drawer completes the action.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming an import with failing checks shows the Override Notes field
test_cases.steps:
1. Run Review on an import that has at least one failing row.
2. Click Confirm.
test_cases.expected: The Confirm drawer opens with a message noting that checks have failed. The Override Notes field is visible and required.

test_cases.scenario: Override Notes field is required when checks have failed
test_cases.steps:
1. Run Review on an import with at least one failing row.
2. Click Confirm.
3. Leave Override Notes blank.
4. Click Confirm in the drawer.
test_cases.expected: The confirm action does not proceed. A validation message indicates that Override Notes are required.

test_cases.scenario: After confirming, the import status changes to Confirmed
test_cases.steps:
1. Confirm a forecast import.
2. Navigate back to the Sprint Forecast page.
test_cases.expected: The team's status badge shows 'Confirmed' (green). The import history table shows the import's status as 'Confirmed'.

test_cases.scenario: Confirmed import is locked — no further edits are possible
test_cases.steps:
1. Confirm a forecast import.
2. Return to the import detail page.
test_cases.expected: The Review, Add Row, and Confirm buttons are disabled. Row-level Edit and Delete actions are not visible. The import is read-only.

test_cases.scenario: Confirm drawer can be cancelled without confirming
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Confirm to open the drawer.
2. Click Cancel.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The import status remains unchanged (Active). No data is locked.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint Forecast page loads within acceptable time on a standard connection
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page on a standard broadband connection.
2. Measure time from navigation to teams panel fully rendered.
test_cases.expected: The teams panel renders within 3 seconds. No visible layout shift occurs after the initial render.

test_cases.scenario: Import detail page renders all rows within acceptable time for large imports
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV with 500+ rows.
2. Open the import detail page.
3. Measure time for the rows table to render.
test_cases.expected: The rows table renders within 5 seconds. Scrolling through rows is smooth with no browser freeze.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint Forecast page is usable on a mobile viewport (375px width)
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page in a browser set to 375px width (or on a mobile device).
2. Inspect the Teams panel and accordion rows.
test_cases.expected: The Teams panel is fully visible. Accordion rows are readable. The Import button and status badge are visible without horizontal scrolling.

test_cases.scenario: Import detail page is usable on a tablet viewport (768px width)
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import detail page at 768px width.
2. Check the rows table and page actions.
test_cases.expected: The rows table is scrollable horizontally if needed. All action buttons are accessible. The tab panel switches correctly.

test_cases.scenario: All interactive elements are keyboard accessible
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page.
2. Use Tab to navigate through accordion rows, buttons, and the Review Complete drawer.
3. Use Enter/Space to activate focused elements.
test_cases.expected: All buttons, accordion toggles, and drawer controls are reachable and operable via keyboard. Focus order is logical.

test_cases.scenario: Check icons in the Rows table have accessible tooltips/aria-labels
test_cases.steps:
1. Run Review on an import with failing rows.
2. Inspect the Checks column icons with a screen reader or by reading the aria-label attributes.
test_cases.expected: Each icon has an aria-label or title attribute describing the check failure (e.g. 'Assignee not found or inactive'). Screen readers can announce the check status.

test_cases.scenario: Page works correctly after a browser back/forward navigation
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page.
2. Navigate to an import detail page.
3. Press the browser Back button.
4. Press the browser Forward button.
test_cases.expected: The Sprint Forecast page shows the correct team accordion state. Navigating forward restores the import detail page with correct data.

test_cases.scenario: API failure during team load shows an error state in the Teams panel
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprint Forecast page while the API is unavailable.
2. Wait for the loading state to resolve.
test_cases.expected: The Teams panel shows an error state with a red icon and the message 'Failed to load teams. Refresh the page to retry.'
